messages.subject: fmultivar package
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I believe the package has a bug in it that when dim=1, the density of t
distribution isn't correct.

Here is the code that shows visually that the density doesn't match the
random variates.

####################

library(fMultivar)

n = 50000
qtile = seq(-5,5,by=0.05)

xtt = rmvst(n,dim=1,df=3)
hist(xtt,300,xlim=c(-5,5),probability=TRUE)
lines(qtile,dmvst(qtile,dim=1,df=3),col='red')

xn = rmvsnorm(n,dim=1)
hist(xn,300,xlim=c(-5,5),probability=TRUE)
lines(qtile,dmvsnorm(qtile,dim=1),col='red')

xt = rt(n,df=3)
hist(xt,300,xlim=c(-5,5),probability=TRUE)
lines(qtile,dt(qtile,df=3),col='red')

####################

I am trying to compare histogram of randomly generated data versus their
corresponding density functions.

The question is regarding "xtt" variable which are random t.
The histogram and the density function doesn't seem to agree.
If you try the others ("xn" and "xt"), you'll see that these "hug the
curve" especially in the beginning part of the tails.
But "xt" seem to be quite a bit off.

Thank you for your help.

Best,

Sang

messages.subject: fGarch
messages.body_plain:
Dear Rmetrics Team,

I have the following problem: Right now I am trying to analyse a time series of heteroscedastic CO2-returns. For the joint estimation of ARMA-GARCH models I want to use the fGARCH package. For selecting the most suitable model I tried to program a loop that reports the AICs and BICs of the ARMA-GARCH estimations. Unfortunately I had to recognize that I cannot extract neither the AICs/BICS nor the Likelihood values. Is there any way to either extract the values or to use another command for calculating them with the given output?
It would be so great if you could help me with this problem.

Thank you so much in advance,

Christoph Hörbelt

messages.subject: Invitation | Global Sustainable Finance Conference, Germany
messages.subject_clean: Invitation | Global Sustainable Finance Conference, Germany
messages.body_plain:
A Two Day International Conference on Sustainable Finance will be held from 5th to 6th of July, 2012 in Karlsruhe, Germany. This event will bring together top executives and senior members of financial institutions, policy makers, sustainable development and environmental management experts, commercial bankers, investment and project finance executives, cleantech and energy industry professionals, academia, senior government officials, representatives of international development institutions and other market players engaged or interested in sustainable finance and green economy. 
 
The delegates will discuss key emerging issues including: climate change, environmental degradation and the emergence of the green economy; the changing role of financial service providers as the economies and financial markets get reshaped; and innovative solutions, success stories and best practices for embedding sustainability in financial institutions. It is a distinctive forum to deliberate on financial innovation and business case to green operations and modify or develop financial products to capitalise on opportunities emerging in numerous sectors, such as in the fields of sustainable infrastructure, energy efficient real estate, green mobility, clean energy production, organic agriculture, green consumer market and in businesses and projects that protect investors, green and enhance financial institutions´ performance and support our transition to low carbon and sustainable economy. 
 
Further to knowledge sharing on issues related to sustainable finance and green economy; the upcoming conference will also help establish partnerships and alliances and in developing synergies. It provides an excellent opportunity to network with the senior members of financial community, multilateral agencies, governmental institutions, academia, sustainable and environmental management practitioners and other stakeholders in Europe and globally. An optional excursion/ get-together will take place on Saturday the 7th of July 2012.
 
You are cordially invited to attend this international event and/ or nominate member(s) of your institution.
 
For further information, please see the event details.
http://etechgermany.com/GSFC_2012.pdf 
Or contact via email: mail at etechgermany.com 
 
Sincerely,
